caveats: High duplication without UMIs cannot be corrected by deduplication; do not attempt read-level dedup on the count matrix — the input is already gene-level counts
Do not drop sample_01 in this step; only characterize it for the modeling step to decide
steps.context: Files: /eval-sonnet-plane-r2-without-total-rna-highdup-n6-2/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 x 13 CSV, first column gene symbol) and .../metadata/metadata.csv (12 x 2, condition column). Design is 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, rRNA-depleted total RNA without UMIs. QC flags duplication >60% in most libraries (expected for total RNA without UMI dedup, not actionable at this stage) and sample_01 at ~4x below median library size.
steps.question: Given the raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata (condition: treated/control, 6 vs 6), what is the library-size distribution, how does sample_01 (flagged at ~4x below median library size) behave relative to its condition group on PCA/sample correlation, and how many genes pass a minimum-count filter for downstream testing?
acceptance_criteria: Reports total counts per sample and confirms sample_01's library size relative to the cohort median
Produces a PCA or sample-correlation plot showing where sample_01 falls relative to its condition group and the other 11 samples
Reports the number of genes retained after a standard low-count filter (e.g. at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples) out of the original 12000
Flags whether sample_01 is an outlier warranting a sensitivity (with/without) DESeq2 run, without unilaterally excluding it

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression, treated vs control, with outlier sensitivity check
caveats: DESeq2 requires raw (non-normalized) integer counts, which is what counts.csv provides — do not pre-normalize before passing to DESeqDataSetFromMatrix
With n=6 per group the outlier sample can materially shift results; report both runs rather than silently picking one
Unpaired single-batch design means no need for a batch or pairing term in the model
steps.context: Raw integer Salmon gene counts, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch — no covariates to adjust for beyond condition. Use the gene filter and sample_01 characterization from T1S1 to decide whether to run only the sensitivity analysis or treat it as primary.
steps.question: Using DESeq2 on the filtered raw count matrix, which genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated (n=6) and control (n=6) heart samples, and is the result sensitive to inclusion/exclusion of the low-library-size sample_01?
acceptance_criteria: Runs DESeq2 Wald test (condition: treated vs control) on the full 12-sample filtered count matrix with default size-factor normalization, producing a table of log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value per gene
Repeats the DESeq2 fit excluding sample_01 (5 vs 6) and reports the overlap of significant genes (padj < 0.05) between the two runs
Reports the number of significant DE genes at padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1 for the primary (all 12 samples) run
States explicitly whether conclusions change when sample_01 is excluded, and recommends which result to treat as primary based on the PCA/correlation evidence from T1S1
Outputs a full results table and an MA/volcano plot for the primary run

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treated vs control DE genes
caveats: GO BP is a nested hierarchy — expect correlated blocks of significant terms rather than independent findings
With only ~12000 background genes in the counts matrix (not full genome), use this gene set as the enrichment background/universe rather than the whole genome
steps.context: Human WikiPathways gene sets (HGNC symbols) at /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt, MSigDB human hallmark at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, MSigDB human GO BP at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-go-human/2026.1/c5.go.bp.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, and MSigDB human canonical pathways (KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID) under /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-canonical-pathways-human/2026.1/. All are HGNC gene symbols matching the human gene-symbol counts matrix, so no ID mapping is needed. Confirm these reference files are present in the environment at run time before use; if any is absent, proceed with whichever pathway sets are available and state which were skipped.
steps.question: Which biological pathways and processes are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control heart samples (from T1S2's primary DESeq2 result)?
acceptance_criteria: Runs over-representation or GSEA-style enrichment on the DESeq2 result (significant gene list at padj<0.05 for ORA, and/or full ranked gene list by log2FC*sign(-log10 pvalue) for GSEA) against human WikiPathways and MSigDB hallmark gene sets
Reports enriched terms with adjusted p-values, and separately for up- and down-regulated genes
Cross-checks top hits against MSigDB human GO Biological Process and canonical pathways (KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID) sets for convergent evidence
Explicitly notes if the DE gene list is small (e.g. <10 genes) and enrichment power is consequently limited

plan.title: Heart treated vs control DE with dedup-robust DESeq2
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples) for a 6-vs-6 unpaired human heart RNA-seq design comparing treated to control, from rRNA-depleted total RNA libraries without UMIs. Two data-quality flags shape the plan: (1) sequencing duplication above 60% in most libraries is expected and largely biological/library-prep artifact for total RNA without UMIs (no UMI-based dedup is possible), so the response is not to attempt read-level deduplication but to confirm at the count-matrix level that library complexity is adequate and to use a count model (DESeq2) whose statistical framework already down-weights genes with unreliable dispersion, plus to run a sensitivity check excluding the extreme low-depth outlier; (2) sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which for a 6-vs-6 design leaves little room to drop a sample without harming power, so the plan first quantifies whether sample_01 is retainable (correlation with its group, PCA position) before deciding to keep-with-caution or exclude. The core analysis is a standard DESeq2 negative-binomial Wald test for treated vs control on raw counts (DESeq2 requires raw integer counts, which this file provides), with QC-driven pre-filtering of low-count genes and explicit reporting of how the outlier sample was handled and its effect on the result (run with and without sample_01 to show robustness). Significant genes are then interpreted mechanistically against WikiPathways human and MSigDB hallmark/GO/canonical pathway gene sets available in the reference store for this organism, using a network-agent-independent enrichment step suited to a ranked/gene-list input. All steps operate on this specific dataset (counts.csv, metadata.csv) and its actual design (6 treated vs 6 control, heart, human, single batch).
